tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee has decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate 50 basis points to 1-1/2 percent.
The recent intensification of the financial crisis has augmented the downside risks to growth and thus has diminished further the upside risks to price stability.
Inflationary pressures have started to moderate in a number of countries, partly reflecting a marked decline in energy and other commodity prices.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 11.88% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.72% and moved +22 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.09% would rise by about $42.83 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 6.1%, and employers added an average of -313k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 5% over the past year (September 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +18 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 1.55% on the day.
